title: Vamana
hook: the small boy grows past the clouds, and asks where to put his third step
tomorrow: a sage's son with a warrior's axe. how did that happen?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Vamana and a warning: Shukra told Bali the boy was Vishnu, and Bali poured the water anyway. A new week starts the moment it touches the ground.

A time-lapse video squeezes a whole season of a seed becoming a tree into a few seconds. This is faster. The water touches the ground, and the boy begins to grow. Past the sacrifice ground, past the clouds, until in the telling the sun and stars are no higher than his waist. One stride covers the earth. A second covers the heavens. Then he turns to the king and asks: where do I put the third?
screen: `THE WATER TOUCHES THE GROUND.` → `HE GROWS PAST THE CLOUDS.` → `TWO STRIDES. EVERYTHING.` → `WHERE DOES THE THIRD GO?`

segments.voice: In the Bhagavata, this giant form is called Trivikrama, the one of the three strides. It's an old picture: a hymn in the Rig Veda already praises Vishnu for measuring out the worlds in three steps. The Purana turns that hymn into a story with a person at the end of it. Two strides have taken everything Bali owns. And Vishnu presses him: you promised three. Bali doesn't argue and doesn't beg. He bows and says: put your third step on my head. Then Prahlada arrives, the boy from the man-lion's story, now Bali's grandfather, and he doesn't grieve. He calls it grace: the riches are gone, and the pride that came with them. Vishnu agrees. He sends Bali to rule Sutala, a world below, and makes a promise that turns the whole story over: he will stand guard at Bali's own door. So the story doesn't end with a king crushed. It ends with a king who ran out of things to give, gave himself, and found Vishnu waiting at his gate. Two strides measure the worlds. The third one measures a person.
screen: `TRIVIKRAMA: THE THREE STRIDES.` · `AN OLD HYMN BECOMES A STORY.` · `PUT IT ON MY HEAD.` · `VISHNU AT BALI'S DOOR.` · then, large: `THE THIRD STRIDE MEASURES A PERSON.`

segments.voice: Bow your head a little and let the back of your neck soften. Rest there for the sit, feeling the weight of your head held, with nothing to defend. If your neck tires, lift it slowly and let your shoulders do the bowing.
Vamana: Vishnu's small form, who grew to stride across the worlds and took his third step on Bali's bowed head.
Keep this one: Vamana, whose third step landed on a bowed head and ended at Bali's door. A new week, begun.

howItsDone: Images of Trivikrama, one foot raised high mid-stride, are carved on temple walls, and in Kerala the festival of Onam welcomes Mahabali back to visit his people.

chat.meaning: Bali bowed and offered himself, and Vishnu met him with a promise to guard his door. Owning it opened the way.

Prahlada.meaning: the boy Narasimha came for; Bali's grandfather
